feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
The discussion focuses on the proposed use of SIGHASH_NONE and its interaction with NOINPUT in Bitcoin script validation. SIGHASH_NONE, rarely encountered, is highlighted for its clever application in this context. The simplification brought by the proposal is noted, particularly in relation to the existing OP_CODESEPARATOR functionality. However, there is uncertainty about whether such an approach would have been considered if OP_CODESEPARATOR had not already existed.
A fundamental concern is raised regarding the security implications of NOINPUT when it does not commit to any input, including scripts or code separators. There is a struggle to understand the original assertion that, without signing the script or masked script, OP_CODESEPARATOR could become unusable or insecure when used with NOINPUT. The central point clarified is that although OP_CODESEPARATOR’s primary function is to influence signature behavior within scripts, its utility diminishes in scenarios where no actual signature occurs through NOINPUT. Beyond the acknowledged risk—arising from reusing keys for multiple outputs—no additional dangers are identified in this usage pattern.
